title: Functions that only compute
summary: The JavaScript is what it is without the attribute.

title: Changing what the function created
summary: A local array and a local ref: nobody else can see them.

title: Changing an argument
summary: The caller's array is not the function's to change.
report: This changes `items`, and `addItem` did not create it.
expected: Array.push changes its first argument, and items belongs to the caller.

title: State outside the function
summary: A ref of the module, and the clock.
expected: Two calls of next can read different values of counter, and Date.now answers differently each time.

title: A function that keeps state
summary: The returned function changes n each time it is called.
report: This function changes `n`, which was created outside it
expected: Each call of counter() is pure, but what it returns is not: the ref outlives the call.

title: Functions of the same file
summary: double passes, trace does not, and the report says where.
expected: Neither helper has an annotation. The compiler looks into both.

title: Function arguments
summary: A pure function may call a function it is given.

title: @mutates
summary: add changes its first argument; fromArray calls it on a buffer it created.

title: JavaScript taken on trust
summary: Externals and a %raw binding, marked by their author.

title: A signature that requires purity
summary: The implementation has no annotation; the signature's is enforced on it.
expected: The signature declares next @pure, so the implementation is checked as if it said so.

title: Module types and functors
summary: Max can call O.compare because Ord says it is pure, and every argument is held to that.

title: A law
summary: Run on a thousand generated carts.

title: Few values: all of them
summary: Two booleans have four values, a light has three.

title: A law that does not hold
summary: The smallest values found that break it.

title: Values of your own types
summary: Trees of every shape, made from the type declaration.

title: A type whose values cannot be made
summary: Only Email can make an Email.t.
report: No value can be made for `email`: `Email.t` is an abstract type
expected: The compiler cannot make an Email.t: the type is abstract, and a made-up string might not be an email the module would accept.

title: Building the value in the law
summary: Take what the value is built from, and a condition as part of the law.
